title: 364-day T-bill bought at a discount, redeemed at par on 14-May-2026 (tax year 2026-27): discount taxed as STCG at slab (alternative view: income from other sources, same tax)
rules: ISIN IN002025Z123: IN00 = Government of India; 'Z' in position 9 = 364-day Treasury Bill (zero-coupon discount instrument)
Convention adopted: a T-bill is treated as a listed security for the 12-month rule (as for G-secs, g30). Here nothing turns on it: 364 days is short-term under either the 12- or 24-month rule
Redemption at maturity extinguishes the bill -> transfer (1961 Act s.2(47)(ii); counterpart in the Income-tax Act 2025 (in force from 1-Apr-2026; tax year 2026-27))
STCG on a non-STT asset: normal slab rates (no s.111A); slab given as 30 %

Alternative view (flagged): the discount on a T-bill is in substance interest/discount income taxable as income from other sources (or interest on accrual, cf. the treatment of deep discount bonds in CBDT Circular 2/2002, as recalled). Tax at slab is identical (1,740.00 + cess); the difference is only the head of income (matters for set-off of capital losses and for reporting). s.2(48) 'zero coupon bond' requires notification and does not cover T-bills
derivation: Redemption at par 2026-05-14: 1,000 @ 100.00 -> proceeds 1,00,000.00. Transfer after 31-Mar-2026 -> Income-tax Act 2025, tax year 2026-27 (fy 2027).
Held 2025-05-15 -> 2026-05-14 = 364 days (not more than 12 months) -> short, slab.
